maria: Quick update from the quant bakeoff this morning — ran AWQ, GPTQ, and FP8 on llama-2-13b with prefix-cache + continuous batching enabled. Found a strange "cache-slope" effect when batch_window > 20: AWQ recovers latency via higher cache hits but has a nontrivial accuracy delta. TL;DR below.

sam: can you share the exact command and raw numbers?

maria: sure — command I used:```
python eval_bakeoff.py --model llama2-13b --quant awq,gptq,fp8 --prefix-cache --cont-batch --batch-window 25 --prefetch=true --seed=42
```
Raw summary (eval set = 8k prompts; metric = EM-like token accuracy):```
Model   acc_drop   cache_hit_delta   p50_lat_ms
AWQ     3.2%       +12.1%            92
GPTQ    1.1%       +4.3%             95
FP8     0.5%       -9.0%             80
baseline (float16, same infra) 0.0%  0.0%            85
```
Notes: cache_hit_delta is relative to baseline float16 with our prefix cache enabled. AWQ's +12% cache hit is concentrated on short-prefix (<=64 tokens) workloads; for long prefixes the hit advantage vanishes.

jackie: interesting — FP8 latency looks best but negative cache delta is worrying. Is that the kv-hash mismatch you flagged earlier?

maria: yep — FP8 path serializes KV keys slightly differently (we found a small endianness/packing mismatch in the quantized KV serializer), which makes prefetcher miss more often. That's fixable but requires a careful migration (backcompat of old cached entries).

nikhil: for AWQ the accuracy drop 3.2% seems high. Is that uniform across prompt types? Could be distributional.

maria: not uniform — breakdown: retrieval QA (short answers) shows ~1.0% drop, code-gen-ish prompts show ~6% drop. Hypothesis: AWQ's per-layer scale approximation hurts pattern-heavy generation. We also see hallucination rate up on longer-gen tasks.

sam: did you try disabling continuous batching to isolate prefix-cache effects?

maria: yes — quick ablation: cont-batch OFF, batch_window:1, prefix-cache ON: AWQ acc_drop -> 3.9%, cache_hit_delta -> +2.2%, p50_lat -> 130ms. So continuous batching amplifies AWQ's cache advantage (higher hit) and lowers latency, but it also seems to expose more accuracy delta in some workloads (we saw 0.7% additional drop on code-gen).

nikhil: so continuous batching is a double-edged sword: helps latency via batching + cache synergy but can magnify quantization artifacts. That squares with my intuition about KV cache alignment across batched requests.

jackie: actionable items?

maria: propose 3 steps: 1) FP8: patch the KV serializer to fix packing; re-run to see if cache delta recovers (low effort). 2) AWQ: run per-layer sensitivity scans (focus on attention/query/project scales) to see which layers cause code-gen regressions. 3) Experiments: instrument per-prefix-length cache hit + accuracy curves and add a runtime policy: for prompt_type=code long-prefix -> prefer GPTQ or float16; for short chat -> AWQ with cont-batch enabled.

ops-bot: CI-benchmark job #bake-1782 finished: artifacts uploaded to gs://redwood-bakeoffs/1782001110/ (profiles, traces, logs).

sam: thanks — can you add the per-prefix-length graphs to the artifact bucket? that's the crucial visualization.

maria: done. uploaded `prefix_hit_by_len.png` and `acc_by_len_quant.png` in that folder. Quick preview: AWQ shows a steep hit curve for len<=64, then a cliff; GPTQ has steady but lower hit; FP8 starts low then slowly increases (once we fix serializer it should jump).

jackie: let's schedule a short triage tomorrow 10am to pick model/runtime policy defaults. I'll invite platform and runtime folks.

maria: sounds good. I'll run the FP8 serializer patch and the AWQ per-layer sweep before then and post updated numbers.

sam: great, thanks — and add a note in the experiment doc with the exact seed/commit so we can reproduce.

maria: done (commit: 3a7f2c9, seed=42).

nikhil: one more ask — include a small test in the prefetcher E2E CI that verifies cached-entry compatibility across quantization format migrations. Saves us surprises when we flip FP8 in prod.

maria: added to queue.

sam: :thumbsup:
